explanation: A prophet in the Old Testament who received God's word and delivered it to the people.
A written text rolled up on a rod, often made of papyrus or parchment. In Jeremiah 36, the scroll is used to record God's message.
A scribe and friend of Jeremiah who wrote down God's words on the scroll at Jeremiah's dictation.
The king of Judah at the time Jeremiah received God's message. Jehoiakim rejected God's warnings and burned the scroll.
An expression of God's strong displeasure with human sin and evil. In Jeremiah 36, God warns of His wrath against Judah and Jerusalem because of their disobedience.
God's righteous punishment for human sin and disobedience. In Jeremiah 36, it is prophesied that God will bring destruction upon Judah and Jerusalem.
A dramatic change or event, often linked to God's intervention in history. In Jeremiah 36, the upheaval is connected to God's judgment on Judah and Jerusalem.
